description: Agent Customs Records: submit customs entry summaries with the commercial invoices and duty payment records they answer to: the importer with its reference, name and currency; each entry with its id, entry number, the shipment or bill of lading it covers, the commercial invoice it declares, the moment filed, the quantity and value declared, the currency and the duty the entry states; each commercial invoice with its id, reference, the quantity and value invoiced and the currency; each duty payment with its id, the entry it pays, the moment paid and the amount. The signed report gives the importer and the entries, each entry against the commercial invoice it names, each declared quantity and value against that invoice, each entry owing duty against a payment recorded, and each shipment against the entry numbers it is entered under, and counts them, and names divergent customs entry records: an entry recorded with no matching commercial invoice, a declared quantity or value that does not match the invoice record, an entry owing duty with no duty payment recorded, and the same shipment entered twice under different entry numbers; then a duty payment naming an entry the records do not hold and duty payments that add to another amount than the duty the entry states, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No entries, no commercial invoices beside the entries, or an entry valued in another currency than its invoice leaves those points unverified. Entries, invoices, shipments and payments match by letters and digits, quantities compare exactly and values to the cent in one currency, the payments for one entry add together, and an entry stating no duty owed reads as duty free. This reads the importer’s own filed entries across shipments: wever_logistics-customs-check reads one cross-border shipment’s customs papers for completeness, while the entry check reads the entries filed against the invoices and the duty paid. Verdict customs_entry_divergent, customs_entry_partial, customs_entry_unverified or customs_entry_consistent. POST /api/customs-entry-check. Reads the customs and trade records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it files no entry, pays no duty, contacts no customs authority or broker and gives no customs or legal advice, which stay with the importer, its licensed customs broker and its advisers, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Customs Records reads an importer’s or exporter’s own customs and trade records: entry summaries, tariff classification records, duty and fee payment records, broker filing records, country-of-origin and marking records, declared-value records, customs bond records and drawback claim records, each against the commercial invoices and duty payment records, the rulings on file, the entries, the importer’s own copies, the origin support on file, the invoices and payments, the entry activity or the duty recorded as paid and the proof on file. The family’s ground is the paper behind the border crossing: what was declared, how it was classified, what duty was paid, and whether the bond and the drawback claims line up; the Agent Tax Records family reads filings made to the tax authority, and the Agent Logistics family reads where a shipment is and when it moves, while this family reads neither. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-customs-records-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-customs-records/.
